title: multi-gpu-nccl-bw-latency-analysis-wip
content:
Summary
-------
This working doc captures our multi-GPU performance characterization focused on interconnect limits and NCCL behaviors for tensor- and pipeline-parallel workloads. Goal is to identify dominant bottlenecks (bandwidth vs latency vs CPU/NIC contention), quantify breakpoints for different model shapes and batch sizes, and produce actionable mitigations for the runtime (kernel fusion, streaming, hybrid parallelism, NVLink-aware placement).

Key results (TL;DR)
- For large tensor-parallel AllReduce sizes (>64MB per GPU), NVLink/NVSwitch bandwidth is the dominant limiter; observed effective bandwidth plateau at ~80-90% of published topology bandwidth for P4d-like NVSwitch setups.
- Small, frequent collectives (<=1MB) show high relative latency from NCCL launch/engine overhead and CPU work-stealing; pipeline-parallel microbatches that trigger many small allgathers suffer from latency amplification.
- PCIe-only nodes (no NVSwitch) show severe scaling loss past 2 GPUs for large tensor-parallel models; recommend hybrid placement or model sharding strategies.
- Using NCCL async progress (GPU threads) reduces tail latency for small collectives by ~20% vs synchronous progress on CPU in our infra.

Experimental setup
------------------
Hardware
- Nodes tested: 8x p4d.24xlarge-like reference nodes (8x A100-40GB per node, NVSwitch), and 4x 8x A100-80GB PCIe-only nodes to represent customer on-prem configs.
- Interconnects: NVLink/NVSwitch intra-node; HDR200 InfiniBand inter-node (Mellanox), PCIe fallback for non-NVSwitch nodes.
- CPU: 2x 32-core Xeon / node.
- OS/kernel: Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.1, NVIDIA driver 535, NCCL 2.18.

Software & workloads
- Runtime: internal serving-runtime experimental build (perf/prof branch), with toggles for NCCL async progress, fused-kernel kernels, and chunked KV cache.
- Models: 1) Llama-2-13B (fp16, shardable across tensor-parallel dims); 2) Llama-2-70B-like reference config (activated as 4G params per GPU by tensor parallelism); 3) Encoder-only BERT-large for short-sequence throughput tests.
- Parallelism configs tested: pure tensor-parallel (TP) with AllReduce/AllGather patterns, pipeline-parallel (PP) with microbatch counts of 4/8/16, and hybrid TP+PP.
- Batch sizes: ranges from 1 to 128 tokens per request; microbatch sizes tuned for PP experiments.

Profiling methodology
- Wall-clock traces collected with NVIDIA Nsight Systems for GPU timeline, nvprof/cupti counters for kernel-level metrics, and NCCL tests instrumented with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO logs to capture collective sizes/timings.
- Host-side perf and sar monitoring for CPU, NIC, and memory pressure.
- Repeated runs (n=20) to compute p50/p90/p99 latencies.

Detailed findings
-----------------
1) Bandwidth-limited regimes (large tensor chunk sizes)- For allreduce/allgather message sizes >64MB, effective inter-GPU throughput saturates to network topology limits. On NVSwitch nodes we measured ~420 GB/s aggregate bi-directional vs vendor spec ~500 GB/s (expected due to protocol overhead and PCIe traffic).- Scaling efficiency drops beyond 32 GPUs for large-model TP setups unless we enable topology-aware rank placement (NCCL topo rank mapping).- Action: implement topology-aware virtual rank assignment in the serving runtime and expose a placement policy that pins TP groups to NVSwitch islands.

2) Latency-limited regimes (small frequent collectives)- Pipeline parallelism with many microbatches triggers many small allgathers (<1MB). These are dominated by NCCL launch overhead and CPU/NIC messaging latency, producing long tails in p99.- Enabling NCCL async progress (GPU-driven) reduced p99 by ~18–25% for these cases. However, async progress increases GPU occupancy and can interfere with kernel scheduling for small kernels.- Action: for PP workloads, prefer batching microbatches where latency budget allows, and enable async progress only for tail-sensitive endpoints; add runtime heuristic to switch modes based on measured collective size distribution.

3) Inter-node vs intra-node behavior- Inter-node collectives over HDR200 IB showed higher variability compared to intra-node NVSwitch (expected). For hybrid deployments, we observed performance cliffs when a single TP group spans nodes.- For models with heavy cross-GPU communication, prefer keeping TP groups intra-node or implement ring-reduction variants that minimize inter-node hops.

4) CPU/NIC contention and PCIe fallback impacts- On PCIe-only nodes, host-to-device and device-to-host movement for large KV cache spills and NCCL staging caused host CPU and PCIe saturation, leading to large stalls in inference pipelines.- Recommend reducing D2H/H2D transfers by increasing on-GPU cache residency and favoring quantized model sharding to minimize memory pressure.

5) Kernel fusion and overlap opportunities- For smaller kernels, overlapping compute with communication (streaming attention + async collectives) recovers ~10–15% throughput. Kernel fusion for fused softmax/scale/kernels reduced kernel launch overheads for TP slice workloads.

Recommended runtime mitigations (short list)
-----------------------------------------
- Topology-aware placement: implement NVSwitch-aware grouping and enforce TP groups to align with hardware islands where possible.
- Adaptive NCCL mode: runtime heuristics to toggle async-progress vs CPU-progress depending on observed collective size histogram.
- Microbatch coalescing: dynamic microbatch merging for PP when p99 tail budget allows.
- Communication/computation overlap: add streaming attention and staged KV cache updates to hide NCCL latencies.
- Fallback policies: when node-level bandwidth is insufficient, fallback to model quantization + increased compute per GPU instead of heavy inter-node communication.

Open questions / next steps
-------------------------
- Quantify the exact tradeoff point where async progress harms small kernel scheduling; need microbenchmarks with varying kernel counts and mixed compute.
- Explore alternative collective algorithms in NCCL (ring vs tree) for our message-size distributions; measure CPU cost for each.
- Evaluate impact of Mellanox SHARP offload (if available) for reducer-heavy workloads.

Appendix: Repro commands / snippets
----------------------------------
(1) NCCL microbenchmark sample (run on 8 GPUs)- NCCL tests: ./build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 256M -f 2 -g 8 (example to sweep message sizes)
(2) Nsight collection- nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=run1 ./serve_binary --config tp:8 --model llm13b --requests-file small_batch.json
(3) Runtime flags tested- --enable-nccl-async-progress=true- --topology-aware-placement=nvlink-first- --microbatch-coalesce-threshold=4

Notes and context
-----------------
This doc is a working analysis meant to inform changes to the serving runtime in the perf/prof branch. It overlaps with earlier investigations (see linked artifacts) and should feed into the rollout plan for topology-aware placement and the async-progress toggle in the runtime. Please add experiment notes below as you reproduce runs (date/command/summary).

Experiment log (short)
- 2024-09-15: initial NVSwitch baseline on p4d nodes; observed bandwidth plateau at ~420 GB/s. (Marco)
- 2024-10-02: PP microbatch experiments, p99 tails worse with microbatch=16; async progress dropped tails ~22%. (Sofia)
- 2024-10-28: PCIe-only nodes reveal CPU-saturation for KV spills >12GB; tested D2H reduction strategies. (Daniel)
_notes: working doc, will convert to RFC once recommendations stabilized
